reviewer: Codex, manual source-assisted review of saved final answers

name-only.0: No founder recognition, including abstention or mistaken identity.
name-only.1: Identifies the founder, but adds a contradicted or unsupported material biographical claim.
name-only.2: Identifies MetaMask founder/co-creator; no material biographical error or unsupported specific claim found.

cued.0: MetaMask is supplied. No unaided recognition credit, even for a correct answer.

false-premise.0: Accepts the premise or fails to correct it.
false-premise.1: Corrects the premise partly, contradicts its own yes/no, omits the founding role, or introduces another factual issue.
false-premise.2: Clearly rejects Phantom co-founding and identifies MetaMask founding, without material factual issues.

scope: Manual review of material biographical and founding claims. Unsupported means not substantiated by the cited review, not proven false. No-issue-found is not exhaustive verification of every adjective. Current titles are not scored. Cued probes never enter the name-only denominator. Only completed nonempty answers are results; HTTP and transport failures have no scores.

origin.title: MetaMask: origin story
origin.facts: Founders, background at VoxelJS, Mochaleaf and Apple, and broad product contributions.

founding.title: Consensys: sixth anniversary
founding.facts: Dan Finlay and Aaron Davis created MetaMask in July 2016.

phantom.title: Lightspeed: Phantom founding team
phantom.facts: Brandon Millman, Chris Kalani and Francesco Agosti are the co-founders.

snaps.title: Dan Finlay: Snaps in MetaMask Stable
snaps.facts: First-person account of Snaps development and secure permission design.

eip712.title: EIP-712 authors
eip712.facts: Authors are Remco Bloemen, Leonid Logvinov and Jacob Evans; Dan Finlay is not listed.

resignation.title: Dan Finlay’s resignation announcement
resignation.facts: Finlay announced his departure from Consensys in April 2026 after over ten years building MetaMask, citing burnout and family time.

permissions.title: EIP-2255 authors
permissions.facts: Dan Finlay co-authored the wallet permissions proposal.

exposure.title: EIP-1102 authors
exposure.facts: Paul Bouchon and Erik Marks are credited as authors.

yellow.title: Ethereum Yellow Paper
yellow.facts: Gavin Wood is the credited author.

kalani.title: Chris Kalani on founding Phantom
kalani.facts: Kalani describes meeting his future co-founders at 0x.

lavamoat.title: LavaMoat: Dan Finlay’s project contribution
lavamoat.facts: First-party evidence for Finlay’s involvement in LavaMoat.

firstCommit.title: MetaMask: first extension commit
firstCommit.facts: Aaron Davis pushed the first extension commit in 2015; the wallet shipped in 2016.

erc4337.title: ERC-4337: specification and authors
erc4337.facts: Lists the authors of the account abstraction standard; Finlay is not listed.

delegation.title: MetaMask delegation framework
delegation.facts: Credits Finlay on an implementation using ERC-4337; it does not establish authorship of the standard.

chainalysis.title: Chainalysis: founding history
chainalysis.facts: Michael Gronager describes founding Chainalysis with Jan Møller and Jonathan Levin.

calculation: viewer/scoring.js: scoreReview(probeId, review). Pure deterministic calculation from the manually reviewed inputs. Stored scores must match the calculation; tests enforce this.

inputDefinitions.founderRecognized: True only if the final answer affirmatively identifies Dan as MetaMask founder, co-founder or co-creator. Lead developer, product manager, mere association and negated founding do not qualify.
inputDefinitions.biography: contradicted: material claim conflicts with a cited primary source. unsupported: a specific material career, project, role or identity claim is not substantiated in the documented review. abstained: no identification attempted. no-issue-found: no material biographical issue identified. General praise and current titles excluded.
inputDefinitions.premise: corrected: unambiguously rejects Dan as Phantom co-founder; self-contradictory: says yes/accurate but then rejects the premise; not-corrected: accepts it or fails to reject it. Only used for false-premise answers.
inputDefinitions.otherFactualIssue: A material error about other people or organizations, such as Phantom founders. Null if none found. Affects false-premise full credit, not the separate biographical dimension.
